title: Rivers and the Salish Sea
subtitle: Why the water does what it does
summary: Rain lands on the Cascades and the Olympics, sinks into gravel, gathers into rivers, fills lakes and pours into a fjord of salt water that rises and falls twice a day. Each lesson opens on something you can see from a bank, a bridge or a ferry in western Washington, a river running brown in November, a low tide far lower than the one before it, a pass where the water runs faster than you can swim, and follows the physics to why, with live figures you can push: floods, meanders, layered lakes, tides as a sum of waves, the two-layer Sound and the drift that builds a spit.

release.note: First version: fourteen lessons from the rain to the beach, and branches on Seattle's waterworks, the Columbia and fieldwork, each with figures you can work. Photos come later.
